gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the bridge unsafe, but it was also far too narrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only was the bridge unsafe' — inverted past simple of be.

gaps.sentence: So loud ___ the music that the neighbours called the police.
gaps.explanation: 'So loud was the music that …' — fronted 'so + adj' with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not since the 1990s ___ unemployment been so low.
gaps.explanation: Not since X has Y happened — present perfect inversion.

gaps.sentence: Scarcely had the plane taken ___ when the alarm sounded.
gaps.explanation: 'Taken off' completes the phrasal verb inside the inverted 'scarcely had … when' structure.

gaps.sentence: Only since the redesign ___ the app gained new users.
gaps.explanation: 'Only since the redesign has the app gained …' — perfect inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not until the second edition ___ the book become a bestseller.
gaps.explanation: 'Not until the second edition did the book become …'.

gaps.sentence: Nowhere ___ you find a better example of Gothic architecture.
Hardly had we left the house ___ it started to pour.
gaps.explanation: Hardly … when — fixed pair; 'than' belongs to 'no sooner'.
